prompt:
Write 7 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a low-speed head-on collision claim, in time order. Injury: concussion. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1197; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant's account changed in important ways between conversations: the direction of the impact and the number of people in the car are now different.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- A neighbor thinks the car was damaged some weeks before the claimed date.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claimant reported a low-speed head-on collision on the day of loss and said she was taken to hospital with a suspected concussion. The driver is named on the policy, and the vehicle was towed from the scene.

Entry 2: Responding officer's report and two independent witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle at the time of the collision, and the other driver gave a consistent account of how it happened.

Entry 3: Photos taken at the scene and the vehicle damage pattern match the described impact and the approximate speed reported. No prior damage to the vehicle is recorded in our file or in the photos supplied.

Entry 4: Claimant called to say she had a headache, nausea and trouble concentrating. She was advised to keep the emergency department discharge notes and any follow-up appointments for the file.

Entry 5: Medical records show a concussion diagnosis, consistent with the kind of force involved. No earlier injury to the same area of the head or neck is known from the records received so far.

Entry 6: In a later call the claimant described the direction of impact differently from her first account and gave a different number of people in the car. The difference has been noted, and the claimant was asked to clarify both points in writing.

Entry 7: A neighbor contacted the desk saying the vehicle looked damaged several weeks before the claimed loss date. The statement is being reviewed alongside the police report, witness statements and the physical damage evidence before any decision is made.
